blurb:
Victor wags with his whole body. Not just the tail. The whole body. That's the thing the volunteers keep coming back to when they describe him, and it's a pretty good summary of who this dog is. He's a five-year-old bulldog mix, 44 pounds, and apparently so happy to spend time with people that he once sat completely still through a bath just soaking up the one-on-one attention. His foster turns the TV on for him when he leaves the house. Victor, it seems, has fully settled into being loved.

He went through the Mostly Mutts Prison Pups training program, so he's been worked with and knows what's expected of him. He does get mouthy and excited when things get rowdy, so kids 15 and up are the better fit. He also prefers being the only dog in the house. He's been through the training, but he's still got a strong personality and some strength behind it.

One more thing worth knowing: his foster is currently helping him work through some leg challenges, so check the medical notes on his profile page before reaching out. The team at Mostly Mutts will walk you through where he stands.

Victor is in a foster home and ready to meet his people. Head to the Mostly Mutts website to submit an inquiry and go from there.

blurb:
Eleven years old and still has a spring in his step. Meeko is a 33-pound Jack Russell/Greyhound mix who came out of animal control and landed in a foster home where he has apparently been thriving ever since. He climbs right into laps. He makes grateful little sighs during baths. He is, by every available measure, a good boy who knows he got lucky and is very happy about it.

He's got some opinions, which honestly feels appropriate for a dog who's been around this long. He wants to be your only dog, not because he's aggressive, but just because that's where he's most comfortable. He'll ignore the neighbor's big dogs from across the yard without a second thought, he just doesn't want to share a household. He can also get vocal when he wants attention, so a house with some space is a better fit than a condo or apartment.

Kids 15 and up are a good match. He got a little nervous around younger kids during his meet and greet at the shelter, so he'd do best in a quieter home. But if you're looking for a calm, affectionate, slightly spunky dog to sit with you in the evenings, Meeko is genuinely hard to beat.

He's currently in a foster home through Mostly Mutts. Submit an inquiry on their website to get the process started.

blurb:
Nine years old, 64 pounds, and somehow still the goofiest dog in the room. Bolton is a hound/boxer mix who came to Mostly Mutts underweight and rough around the edges, but you'd never know it now. His foster says he lights up every room he walks into, and that tracks. He's been through the Mostly Mutts Prison Pups training program, so he's not just charming, he's got some skills to back it up.

His energy is the best kind of senior energy. He'll sniff every inch of a trail with full hound commitment, then come home and happily park himself next to you on the couch. No drama. Just a sweet, loyal dog who had a hard start and is clearly grateful for the second chance.

A couple things to know: no cats, since he'll chase them. He's been great with kids around 8 to 12 in his foster home, but toddlers would be a tough fit since he's a big guy and could accidentally knock them over. Dogs are fine, he actually loves greeting them on walks. If you've got a dog-friendly house and a couch with room for one more, Bolton is worth meeting.

blurb:

She's two and a half months old, part of the shoe-themed sibling group at Mostly Mutts, and she takes the longest to warm up of the bunch. Here's the thing though. She's also curious about everything. She wants to know what's happening, who you are, and what that thing in your hand is. She just prefers to figure it out on her own timeline. Once she decides you're okay, the foster says she turns playful and adventurous. Chasing toys, wrestling with her siblings, finding the best high spots in the room. She's a real kitten underneath the caution, she just needs a patient person to draw it out.

She recently moved to the Kitty Room at the shelter, so you can go meet her in person now. She'd do best in a quieter home with adults or older, gentle kids. No rough handling and no sudden movements. If you have another calm cat at home, that could actually help her settle in faster.

Mostly Mutts is in Kennesaw. Head to mostlymutts.org to start the process or stop in during adoption hours to say hello.

blurb:

He loves playtime, chasing toys, wrestling with his siblings, and climbing whatever he can get his paws on. He's litter trained, which is a nice bonus at this age. He also gets along with the ferret in his foster home, which honestly just adds to the charm.

He'd do best with older, gentle kids since sudden movements still startle him a bit. And if you already have a cat at home who might enjoy a small chaotic roommate, Loafer would probably love that too.

blurb:

She was pregnant when she arrived, went straight to a foster home, and raised four kittens there. Some of those babies already have homes now. Boots is next, and she has earned it.

She's an independent girl, which means she's not going to follow you room to room demanding attention. She does her own thing, and when she's ready for company, she'll find you. Comes over for pets, sits in your lap for a while, then goes back to her spot. If you've ever had a cat who respected your personal space while also expecting you to respect hers, you already know this personality type and you probably loved it.

One thing to know: she can get overstimulated during petting and will give a little nip to let you know she's done. Not aggressive, just communicating. Her foster figured out her signals quickly and says they get along great. She'd do best with adults or older kids who understand cat body language and won't push past her limits.
